Choose the Supply Route for Your Bulk Order

Start with what the receiving team needs: individual pieces for distribution, multiple designs on a sheet, or printed labels for repeated application. Keep quantity per design separate from the combined total so the quote describes the stock you actually need.

For a wholesale or repeat project, include artwork versions, final dimensions, surface, delivery format, packing and destination. Pricing, material suitability, order quantity and timing are confirmed for the actual project; a sample image does not establish those terms.

Build a Packaging Label Brief Around the Finished Pack

For custom product labels, show the filled bottle, jar, pouch or box and mark the usable panel. Identify the surface finish, seams, opening features and any viewing area that must stay clear. A flat artwork file cannot establish the space available on the assembled package.

Choose roll labels when the project needs roll supply for the intended application route; compare sheets or individual pieces where the packing task calls for them. Format does not establish adhesive suitability. Record conditions at application separately from moisture, cold, oil or handling later in use.

Send approved front/back artwork, dimensions, quantity per SKU, application method and destination through the project brief. The product owner supplies and approves ingredients, claims and required copy. Construction, proof scope and commercial terms need project-specific confirmation.

/products/custom-die-cut-stickers/.Section:
Project decisions

Count Finished Pieces and Define the Packed Set

A contour cut and a retail set are separate instructions. State how many accepted pieces of each design belong in a bag, backing-card set or bulk group. Identify designs and quantities so a combined print total cannot be mistaken for complete sets.

Show the full cut outline and any narrow protrusions at final size. If a larger backing area is useful for peeling or additional print, compare a kiss-cut arrangement rather than stretching a die-cut description. Material and outdoor or wet-use requirements still need their own construction review.

/products/custom-kiss-cut-stickers/.Title: Custom Kiss-Cut Stickers | Cutline & Backing Review
/products/custom-kiss-cut-stickers/.Description: Specify custom kiss-cut stickers with retained backing, usable peel space and final-size cutlines. Choose individual backed pieces or a multi-design sheet layout.
/products/custom-kiss-cut-stickers/.Section:
Project decisions

Approve Two Shapes: the Sticker and Its Backing

Mark the peelable artwork contour and outer backing as separate boundaries. The backing can carry an intentional grip area or additional design, but its dimensions must not be mistaken for the finished sticker size. Review small projections and peel access at physical size.

Kiss-cut describes the cut relationship; it does not tell the supplier how many designs form a sheet or set. For multiple stickers on one backing, continue to the sheet page and supply the sheet size, component count and sheets per pack. For an individual giveaway, specify the backed piece and its packed quantity.

/products/custom-roll-labels/.Title: Custom Roll Labels | Printed Packaging Label Rolls
/products/custom-roll-labels/.Description: Custom printed roll labels for bottles, jars, boxes and bags. Confirm surface, size, quantity per SKU, core and unwind details for a project-specific quote.
/products/custom-roll-labels/.Section:
Project decisions

Connect the Printed Label to the Application Station

Send a filled-pack photo, label width and height, surface material and quantity for every artwork version. Explain whether the label is applied by hand or with an applicator. Keep conditions at application separate from later storage, cleaning or condensation.

For machine use, provide the equipment reference, core inner diameter, permitted roll outer diameter and a labeled unwind diagram showing the leading edge. Do not rely on a winding number without the supplier’s matching diagram. Include any label gap or sensing requirement specified by the equipment owner.

Confirm which data is printed with the label and which is added later. A batch field needs the actual printing method and finished surface reviewed; a light-colored box alone is not an overprint specification. Materials, protective finish, sample scope and order terms remain subject to confirmation.

/products/custom-sticker-sheets/.Title: Custom Sticker Sheets | Multi-Design B2B Printing
/products/custom-sticker-sheets/.Description: Plan custom sticker sheets with multiple designs, usable peel spacing and counted sets. Send sheet dimensions, cutlines and quantities per sheet version.
/products/custom-sticker-sheets/.Section:
Project decisions

Release a Countable Sheet, Then a Complete Set

List each sticker design, its finished dimensions and the required number on the supplied sheet. Mark the outer backing, cutlines, margins and usable peel spacing on one final-size reference. A layout that fits on screen can leave a small sticker difficult to lift after cutting.

State whether the order quantity counts sheets, individual stickers or retail packs. If a pack needs two different sheet versions, identify both and their quantities; one total does not show the intended split. Review the smallest functional piece and longest text before freezing the layout.

Kiss-cut is the cutting method commonly used for these layouts, while a sticker sheet is the delivered grouping. Keep the two decisions connected without treating them as interchangeable product briefs. Send original or authorized artwork, quantities by sheet version and bag/header-card requirements for review.

/products/custom-holographic-stickers/.Title: Custom Holographic Stickers | Artwork & Finish Review
/products/custom-holographic-stickers/.Description: Plan custom holographic stickers with defined reflective areas, white-ink intent and final-size artwork. Compare a physical finish reference before bulk approval.
/products/custom-holographic-stickers/.Section:
Project decisions

Approve Where the Reflective Effect Remains Visible

Provide a marked artwork reference for exposed reflective areas, color coverage and any proposed white printing. Important text should remain readable in the intended view; an attractive rainbow appearance on a screen cannot establish how the physical finish changes with light.

Use a relevant physical material or printed reference to discuss the finish, with its construction and limitations identified. Keep dimensions, cut method, quantity per design and packing in the brief. A decorative holographic effect is not an authentication system and does not establish outdoor life, waterproof performance or a certification.
